gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-fs-epilogue: Espresso Dolce writes in a glowing, calligraphic hand, like neon tubing. Epilogue follows in curvy sans with a tall lowercase and a wire-thin stroke, which keeps long paragraphs feeling loose and unhurried.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-general-sans: Understated and a little decorative, Espresso Dolce leans on a calligraphic hand with wide-eyed lowercase e shapes. General Sans then fills the line with a tall x-height and smooth curves, so extended reading glides along without a snag.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-satoshi: Approachable from the start, Espresso Dolce sets a calligraphic script with a neon-tube thickness against Satoshi's soaring, uniformly cut sans-serif lowercase. Paragraphs stay open and easy.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-switzer: Espresso Dolce is calligraphic and tube-thick, like neon glass. Next to it, Switzer's tall, wire-like sans-serif letters feel crisp and Swiss, so the script reads as the playful one and the body as the straight-faced one.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads bookish and graceful, its serif strokes shifting gently in weight, with wide channels running into each counter. Ethnocentric's wide-set display letters add speed above it.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-lora: Literary Lora brings a classic serif with a broad, welcoming c and only slight hairline thinning at its curves, giving Ethnocentric's fast, aggressive display letters something bookish to push against. They make a lively headline-and-text team.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-noto-serif: Fast, wide, and loud: that's Ethnocentric, with short ascenders over big bowls and letters pushed apart. Noto Serif settles in beneath as a text serif with a prominent x-height, and if the heading is made small, its speed starts to feel cramped.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-cascadia-code: Industrial and chunky, Existence has wide, porthole-like counters and terminals cut short of the bowl, then hands off to Cascadia Code's thin, wire-like sans-serif, where every letter keeps its distance. Long lines read smooth and spaced.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board. Existence is the one that makes an entrance with its heavy, porthole-open shapes, while the sans body does the quieter job of keeping text compact and consistent.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-julius-sans-one: Clean and open, Julius Sans One spaces its letters generously. Its strongest quality against Existence is the tension between that airy, open-ended sans-serif and the heading's heavy, industrial porthole counters.
